rv.q: While the perhaps intentional murkiness of Walker’s script leads to more questions than answers, it may be enough this spooky season that it does provide some spine-tingling scares, especially in this well-mounted, well-acted production.
The taut, entertaining production locates its deepest terrors not in supernatural forces but in the harm people inflict on one another.

There’s a question, implicitly asked and chillingly answered, in the gripping SpeakEasy Stage Company production of Walker’s layered gothic drama: How far would you go to get what — or whom — you want?
Now on the Speak Easy Stage , "COVENANT " can thrill, entertain and, above all, scare the bejeezus out of Boston audiences thanks to the creative efforts of Speak Easy director Dawn M. Simmons .
Walker’s narrative is rife with the kind of feverish religion and unbridled gossip that combine to create their own mythology, distorting reputations and disrupting lives.
Few are likely to be bored by this production, but many may be hard-pressed to explain the ending or the meaning of what they have seen.
Covenant is a curious beast; it has little scares and big surprises.
